summary: When a whole page cannot be shown — it does not exist, this account may not see it, it failed to load or render, or there is no connection — the page says which, inside the shell, with a way forward.
useWhen: a route has no page: an unknown address, or a record that does not exist (404)
the page exists and this account may not open it: a shared link, an old bookmark, a role that changed (403)
the page's own data failed to load, or the page threw while rendering (500)
there is no connection and the page has nothing loaded to show

useInstead.when: a region of a page failed and the rest works
useInstead.use: EmptyState with `reason="error"` and `size="panel"` in that region
useInstead.why: replacing a working page because one card failed takes away everything that did load

useInstead.when: the page loaded and is empty — no records yet, or none match
useInstead.why: nothing to show is not an error, and calling it one tells the user something broke

useInstead.when: the connection drops on a page that already loaded
useInstead.why: what is on screen is still true and still readable; a full-page error would throw it away

structure: Inside the PageShell, never instead of it: the Header, the navigation and any Banner stay, and only <main> is replaced. The one exception is a failure above the shell itself — then a plain page with the product's name, the sentence and a Reload link, because nothing else is left to render.

A PageHeader whose title names what could not be shown — "Page not found", "Settings", "Agent" — with the same `titleId` the route's page uses, so <main aria-labelledby> and the shell's focus-on-navigate work unchanged. Never "Error" or "Oops".

Beneath it an EmptyState, `size="page"`, `headingLevel={2}`, with the reason that is true: `no-results` for 404, `no-access` for 403, `error` for a failed load, a crash or no connection. Its title says what happened in the user's words; its description says what it means for them and what is unaffected.

`action` is the one thing most likely to fix it: a way back to a list for 404, a way to ask for access for 403 (who to ask, by name or role), Try again for a failed load, Reload page for a crash. `secondaryAction` is a Link somewhere that works — the section's list, or the overview.

A failed load or a crash shows a reference the user can quote to support — "Reference err_7Q2KX" — with a CopyButton beside it. The same reference goes to the error log. Never a stack trace, an exception name or an HTTP code on its own.

A crash is caught by an error boundary around the route's content, inside the shell and keyed by the route, so navigating away clears it. Reload page resets the boundary; it does not reload the browser unless resetting fails again. A page whose code could not download — a lazily loaded chunk, offline — is not a crash: show the offline kind, and reload rather than reset, because a browser may remember the failed import.

No connection: `navigator.onLine` and the `online` / `offline` events. While offline, a Banner in the shell says so on every page. A page that could not load because of it shows the offline kind — "You're offline" — and tries again by itself when the connection returns, as well as on Try again.

403 or 404 for a record that exists but is hidden: 404, unless the user can already know it exists. Saying "you don't have access to Payroll agent" to someone who guessed the ID tells them there is a Payroll agent.

Navigation does not offer what the account cannot open: an item the role cannot enter is hidden, not shown and then refused. The 403 page is for arriving anyway — by a link, a bookmark, a role changed mid-session.

When the page is rendered by a server, it returns the matching status — 404, 403, 500, or 503 when a service it needs is down — so crawlers and monitoring see what the user sees. Offline has no status: no request reached a server.

not-found.title: There is no page at this address — or, for a record, "There is no agent with this ID"
not-found.action: a Link back to the list the record would be in

no-access.title: "You don't have access to workspace settings"
no-access.action: who can grant it — "Ask a workspace admin", with the admin's name when the product knows it

failed.title: "This agent couldn't load" for data; "Something went wrong on this page" for a crash
failed.action: Try again, or Reload page for a crash, with the reference and its CopyButton

offline.title: "You're offline"
offline.action: Try again; the page also retries on its own when the connection returns

loading.must: While Try again or Reload page runs, keep the error on screen and put a Spinner in the action — or show the page's own loading state once the retry has started. Never blank <main> between the error and the answer.
loading.why: a page that goes blank on retry looks like the retry broke it, and a user who looks away comes back to nothing

empty.must: A page that loads and has nothing is not this pattern: show the page, and an EmptyState for its content with `first-run` or `no-results`.
empty.why: an error message over an empty but working page tells the user their data is gone

error.must: When the retry fails too, stay on the error with a new reference and the same actions. Do not retry in a loop; after the connection returns, retry once.
error.why: an automatic loop hides the failure behind a spinner and hammers a service that is already down

requires: the PageHeader's `titleId` on <main aria-labelledby>, as on every page — the error page is the page
the document title set for the error — "Page not found · Ops" — so a tab and the history say what happened
the connection's change said through a `role="status"` region the shell always renders — "You're offline", then "Back online" — because a Banner inserted with its message is not reliably announced
notes: No `role="alert"` on the page: arriving at an error is reading a page, and the shell's focus-on-navigate already takes the user to its heading.
Retrying on `online` changes the page under the user; the page's own loading state announces it, and the offline Banner going away says the connection is back.

antiPatterns.dont: a full-screen error that replaces the Header and navigation
antiPatterns.do: the PageShell pattern, with this in <main>
antiPatterns.why: the navigation is how the user gets somewhere that works; without it the only way out is the browser's back button
not found, no access, a failed load and no connection each have a different fix, and one message hides which the user needs

antiPatterns.dont: a stack trace, an exception name, or a bare "Error 500"
antiPatterns.do: a sentence, and a reference to quote
antiPatterns.why: the user cannot act on it, and support cannot find it without the reference

antiPatterns.dont: redirecting an unknown address to the home page
antiPatterns.why: the user never learns the link was wrong and keeps using it

antiPatterns.dont: a 403 for a record the user could not already know exists
antiPatterns.why: confirming that an ID exists is itself a leak
